native_result.query: In which millenium did amber had the highest value and in what time interval did it peak?
native_result.HypoA: Amber has historically high and stable values in the 4th millenium BCE. with its all time peak around 3300 to 3000BCE.
native_result.HypoB: Amber had its highest value in the 4th millennium BCE (4000-3001 BCE, ~6050-4951 calBP; equivalently the calBP bin 5001-6000), where its mean Z-score is +1.49 versus +0.18 for the next-best covered millennium, and it peaked during the interval ~3300-3000 BCE (~5250-4950 calBP). At that maximum the amber Z-score is pinned at +1.54 for a continuous ~300-year plateau (so no single peak year is defined; boundaries are only precise to +/-1 century because the underlying data are 100-year anchors), and smoothed (50-250 year rolling-mean) peaks all fall inside that same window. Amber's high stand is broader than the plateau - Z >= 1.4 from about 4000 to about 2990 BCE - and corresponds to the EN-to-MN (early Funler/Funnel Beaker) transition; afterwards amber collapses to Z ~ -0.28 (3rd millennium BCE) and Z ~ -0.56 (2nd millennium BCE), where Copper & Gold becomes the dominant capital form (mean Z +0.90 in the 2nd millennium BCE). 'Highest value' here means maximum archaeological prominence/incidence Z-score, not economic price; pollen openness (Belau_PC1, pollen_inter_100) and the KDE population proxy are only slightly elevated in the peak window (1.02 vs 0.87 and 3.69e-4 vs 2.61e-4) and their correlations with amber change sign between windows, so they are context, not explanation.
native_result.WorkflowB: 1) Load all three CSVs (capital/pollen with decimal=','); verify alignment: 3601 contiguous annual rows, calBP+CE=1950 everywhere. 2) Same-series / year-0 test: capital Zamber, ZCU_AU, ZMonument matched ts Amber, CopperGold, MonumentCount 37/37 exactly under CE=-BCE and 0/36 under CE=-(BCE-1), establishing capital.csv as the 100-yr anchor grid of the same series and requiring no year-0 correction; ts.pollen confirmed identical to Belau_PC1. 3) Coverage audit: raw Amber 37 non-null / 3564 NaN at century anchors; Amber_inter gap-free. 4) Primary metric = millennium-wise mean of Amber_inter under three binnings (BCE-ceil primary, BCE-floor, calBP-ceil) plus an independent anchor-level table from capital Zamber; partial edge millennia reported both included and excluded. 5) Peak described as (a) exact-max plateau interval in CE and calBP, (b) explicit +/-1-century resolution limit, (c) centered rolling-mean peak centres for 50/100/150/200/250 y, (d) sustained-high intervals at named thresholds (max-0.1=1.44, 1.40, 1.50, 90th pct, 1.00). 6) Secondary descriptive cross-checks only: social-capital triad (Amber vs Copper&Gold vs Monument Count) millennium means and full-window vs peak-window correlations; pollen openness (raw Belau_PC1, pollen_inter_100, pollen_grate_100) and kde_all_mean likewise. No causal modelling performed.

Malformed judge output raises an evaluation error; no hidden retries.
evaluator_config.aggregation: recall_context * mean_accuracy_score; unmatched predicted contexts stay in denominator
evaluator_config.native_behavior_preserved: Variable/relation comparisons receive full hypotheses for each matched context pair.

details.score_scope: Reference agreement of submitted hypothesis; execution is not independently verified by this native metric.
